summary: OpenAI published a builder's guide describing how startups use GPT-5.6's model family, reasoning-effort controls, and new Responses API primitives (retained reasoning/compaction, native multi-agent orchestration, programmatic tool calling, extended prompt caching) to build cheaper and more efficient agents.

mechanisms.reason: The document states a stated technique (smaller distilled models plus tunable reasoning effort) delivering near-identical benchmark performance at a small fraction of the compute cost.
mechanisms.quote: At launch, GPT‑5.6 Luna (Extra High) delivers essentially the same performance, scoring 84.04% at a cost of $1.33.

mechanisms.reason: OpenAI describes native multi-agent orchestration in the API that coordinates parallel agent workstreams to complete tasks, shifting execution from single model calls to delegated multi-agent work.
mechanisms.quote: using native multi-agent orchestration allows coordinating multiple agents across parallel workstreams to finish complex tasks faster.

practices.reason: GPT-5.6's smaller models match or approach prior flagship accuracy on agentic and reasoning benchmarks at dramatically lower cost, changing which model tier a team should default to.
practices.quote: Luna keeps 98% of GPT‑5.5’s extraction accuracy at one-eighteenth the cost.

practices.reason: Programmatic tool calling, retained reasoning/compaction, and native multi-agent orchestration are concrete, implementable architectural patterns with stated token and score gains.
practices.quote: the score jumped to 38.3%—while using roughly 6× fewer output tokens.

practices.reason: Extended prompt cache TTL and deterministic cache breakpoints are directly reproducible techniques to cut input token cost and latency on the caller's own stack.
practices.quote: Across the entire family of models, the prompt cache TTL has been extended to a minimum of 30 minutes and cache breakpoints can now be set deterministically within a model’s context window.

practices.reason: The ARC-AGI-3 harness investigation and benchmark comparisons (BrowseComp, Agents' Last Exam) show a methodology for measuring reasoning-effort and architecture trade-offs, though it is the lab's own harness and unreplicated externally.
practices.quote: You can read more on our ARC-AGI-3 harness investigation here.

notable_reason: The guide documents a roughly 25x cost reduction for equivalent benchmark performance (BrowseComp: $33.27 to $1.33) driven by model-family redesign and reasoning-effort tuning, a concrete inference-cost datapoint for infrastructure watchers.
